previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with chronic pancreatitis was admitted with worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She had recently been in a motor vehicle collision and had residual seatbelt-related abdominal discomfort. Imaging revealed a partial small-bowel obstruction likely due to adhesions from a prior C-section, with no evidence of acute pancreatitis. She was managed conservatively with bowel rest, IV fluids, pain control, and antiemetics. Her symptoms improved with passage of gas, bowel movements, and successful advancement to a full diet. She also reported new-onset headaches, which were managed with continuation of home medications. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned with her primary care provider and gastroenterologist.

Brief Hospital Course:
Pt is a ___ y.o female with h.o chronic pancreatitis, presumed 
sphincter of oddi dysfunction, anxiety/depression, hearing 
impairment who presented with 2 day h.o epigastric pain with 
nausea and vomiting.
.  
#acute on chronic pancreatitis-Per outpt GI, etiology presumed 
to be due to sphincter of oddi dysfunction. Pt reported that 
presenting symptoms were similar to prior flares of 
pancreatitis. Lipase was elevated on admit; KUB did not show 
evidence of obstruction/free air. Initially, pt was made NPO and 
given IVF. She was given medication for pain and nausea IV prn. 
Outpt GI provider was emailed of pt's admission and plan is to 
perform MRCP with secretin as an outpatient for further 
evaluation. Pt was continued on home nitroglycerin, mylanta and 
H2 blocker. Her diet was gradually advanced to regular, low fat 
and she did not report any pain or nausea. Pt did not require 
any pain medication on day of discharge. Pt advised to avoid 
alcohol. Pt will be following up with her outpt GI for further 
care. Pt was wondering whether she should resume/restart 
rifaximin. This question was deferred to the outpatient setting.
.  
#drowsiness-On admission, likely medication effect from opioids, 
benzos, antiemetics. Pt reported that ""this occurs during her 
admissions"". Decreased dose of pain medication and symptoms 
improved/resolved. Tox screen was performed given drowsiness and 
returned positive for amphetamines-but suspect crossreaction 
with medications (?H2 blocker) as pt does not clinically appear 
to be using amphetamines. However, drowsiness could have been 
due to amphetamine withdrawal. Tox positive for benzos, but pt 
was taking at home.  
.  
#depression/anxiety-no current signs of SI. Continued home 
regimen of fluoxetine, trazodone, clonazepam. Prazosin for night 
terrors  
.  
#normocytic anemia-baseline 36-40. 35.3 on day of discharge. 
currently. No signs of bleeding were present.
.
